title: Songwriting and Composition
intro: Theory explains how music works; this topic is about using it to make your own. It follows a song from the first idea to a finished, arranged piece, at the piano and on the guitar, and points back to the Music Theory and Guitar Theory pages whenever a technique rests on a theory idea.

blocks.text: There is no single right starting point. Songwriters commonly begin from one of these, then build the rest around it:

items: A melodic hook: a short phrase you can sing, often the title line.
A chord progression or a riff: four chords on the piano, a figure on the guitar.
A groove: a rhythm or a drum pattern that sets the feel.
A lyric or title: an idea, a phrase, a story.
A sound: an instrument, a tuning, a texture.

blocks.text: Whatever comes first, record it immediately (a phone voice memo is enough). Most ideas are lost between having them and writing them down.

items: Sketch: find the core idea and its key, tempo and feel.
Expand: write a contrasting section (a chorus for a verse, a bridge for both).
Structure: arrange sections into a form (see Song Structure (#/arts/songwriting/song-structure)).
Arrange: decide what each instrument plays (see Piano and Guitar Together (#/arts/songwriting/piano-and-guitar-together)).
Finish: write a lead sheet or chart and make a recording (see Finishing a Song (#/arts/songwriting/finishing)).
Writing Melodies (#/arts/songwriting/melody): contour, range, motives, rhythm and hooks.
Chord Progressions (#/arts/songwriting/chord-progressions): choosing chords, harmonising a melody, borrowed colours.
Rhythm and Groove (#/arts/songwriting/rhythm-and-groove): tempo, feel and the grooves of common styles.
Song Structure (#/arts/songwriting/song-structure): verses, choruses, bridges, contrast and lyrics.
Writing at the Piano (#/arts/songwriting/at-the-piano): accompaniment patterns and voicings.
Writing on the Guitar (#/arts/songwriting/on-the-guitar): strumming, fingerpicking, riffs and tunings.
Piano and Guitar Together (#/arts/songwriting/piano-and-guitar-together): arranging both instruments so they support each other.
Finishing a Song (#/arts/songwriting/finishing): lead sheets, charts and a simple home recording.

blocks.text: Most of this topic needs only the basics: major and minor keys (#/arts/music-theory/scales-and-keys), triads and seventh chords (#/arts/music-theory/chords), harmonic function and cadences (#/arts/music-theory/harmony) and popular forms (#/arts/music-theory/form/popular-forms). Guitarists should also know chord voicings (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/chord-voicings) and progressions on the guitar (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/harmony-and-progressions).

Sources: Perricone, J. (2018). Great Songwriting Techniques. Oxford University Press; Webb, J. (1998). Tunesmith: Inside the Art of Songwriting. Hyperion; Pattison, P. (2009). Writing Better Lyrics, 2nd ed. Writer's Digest Books.
